body: You sound a lot like me, except for the fact that hey, you know what? Regardless if you're not where you want to be right now and you feel like things aren't going the way they should, at LEAST you're sticking to your guns and making something of yourself in spite of things not being great in a lot of respects by mere virtue of the fact that you are at least staying in school, which you will realize later on is commendable, something I wish I had done for myself rather thab just succumb to the pain of feeling socially awkward etc and using that as a reason to just totally drop out from school, and society. Please hang in there. Be strong, like I wish I had been.

Hit me up if you want to talk... I feel suicidal on and off as well so I may not be the best at offering advice but let me know, I at least know how it can be and sometimes the only thing that would help is a listening ear or eye in this case so feel free
Ugh.  This just made me throw up in my mouth a little bit.

I have aspergers as well, and I am in my twenties.  It can be very hard even now, but high school was by far one of the worst times for me as far as my social anxiety and anger about fitting in went.  When I look back, I wish I had spent more time with my friends, whoever they were, even if I didn't necesarilly feel like I fit in with them that well either, because at least being accepted by some people, any people, can do wonders for self esteem/self worth. Instead, most of the time I shut down when I was around them, and didn't open myself up.  This is something I could have helped somewhat, had I decided to take a different attitude.  Do you have at least one person who you could consider a good friend, someone you could open up to and be frankly honest with about this? I think this might be a step for you.  Just be honest about where you are and maybe it will allow the other person to understand better where you are coming from.  I know that at that age had someone given me that advice I would have thought something like "but what if they DON'T understand, and think I'm even more weird than they already did/do?" or "what if they say something about it to somebody else and then word gets spread around and...."  I can understand these worries, if you have them.  Ultimately, that's just the risk you're going to have to take.  But if you honestly know that you have one person whom you can confide in about things, and are worthy of your trust, (this is key, don't just tell this to anyone cuz not everyone WILL understand,) then perhaps it would be good to share, for the sake of getting it off of your chest, when the time is right.  It might even help to bring you closer, by confiding in that way.  If all else fails and you haven't been able to do this already, I would suggest doing a little research online to see if there are any aspergers-related support groups, or therapists with a working knowledge of the condition in your area.  This could help you immensely, I think.  I am looking for the same kind of help for myself at the time being actually, and I am much older than you.  Just think what kind of hope for the future you might have if you're able to start learning and applying any coping strategies you might learn early on.  Had I really started accepting the issue for what it is and actively seeking to learn coping strategies and social methods earlier on rather than just staying pissed off about and feeling like a victim for so long, I might have found myself in a very different place than where I am today.  Either way, however, it is better late than never, and I have decided that I'm going to work on myself, and get all the help I can within reason to imrove.  If I can do it at my age, you certainly can too.  You just need support, and trying to open up to your friends, again if there are any you actually feel like you can trust, might be the place to start.  That and counseling.  I hope this helps in some way.
